name: AA-LCR

evaluation.harbor_aligned_metric: accuracy (pass@1). A Harbor adapter is in flight at https://github.com/harbor-framework/harbor/pull/1397 (OPEN as of April 2026). It evaluates 99 of 100 tasks (task 2 excluded for an unfixable ground truth error; tasks 40 and 94 ship with corrected answers) and uses GPT-5-mini as the LLM equality judge rather than AA's Qwen3 235B. Cleanest parity run: codex@0.117.0+gpt-5-mini scored 0.687 (68/99) on Harbor vs 0.68 for gpt-5-mini on AA's direct-LLM leaderboard (2026-04-10). Three other parity runs (claude-code@2.1.104+claude-haiku-4-5, terminus-2@2.0.0+gpt-5-mini, terminus-2@2.0.0+claude-haiku-4-5) diverge more widely because AA-LCR has no native agent harness, and the scaffold choice has a large effect on long-context document QA.

notes:
AA-LCR is Artificial Analysis's long context reasoning benchmark. It ships 100 human-crafted questions that each require reading roughly 100K input tokens and then reasoning across several documents to arrive at a single correct answer. The dataset draws from seven real-world document categories: company reports, industry reports, government consultations, academic papers, legal documents, marketing materials, and survey reports. In total the corpus is about 3M tokens spanning 30 document sets and 234 documents.

Scoring is pass@1 accuracy. A candidate answer is compared against a human-verified reference by an LLM equality checker (Qwen3 235B A22B 2507 in non-reasoning mode). That design avoids brittle string matching but does introduce some dependence on the judge model. Human first-attempt accuracy is reported at 40 to 60 percent, which is why the task remains hard even for specialists.

AA-LCR is one component of the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index. There is no academic paper or public code repository, so the `paper` and `github` fields are null. The announcement blog (https://artificialanalysis.ai/articles/announcing-aa-lcr) and the Intelligence Benchmarking methodology page (https://artificialanalysis.ai/methodology/intelligence-benchmarking) are the canonical technical references. A Harbor adapter (harbor-framework/harbor PR #1397, OPEN as of April 2026) wraps the benchmark for agent evaluation. It runs 99 of the 100 tasks, swaps in GPT-5-mini as the LLM equality judge, and records four parity runs in its `parity_experiment.json` covering codex, claude-code, and terminus-2 scaffolds.
